'''Great Saint James''' is a [[private island]] in the [[United States Virgin Islands]], located off the east end of [[Saint Thomas, U.S. Virgin Islands|St. Thomas]] and belonging to subdistrict [[East End, Saint Thomas, U.S. Virgin Islands|East End, Saint Thomas]]. The island is approximately {{convert|165|acre|ha}} in size,<ref name=":0" /> and is located {{convert|0.4|km|mi}} southeast of [[Saint Thomas, U.S. Virgin Islands|Saint Thomas]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Campbell |first1=Earl W. |title=The Effect of Introduced Roof Rats on Bird Diversity of Antillean Cays |journal=[[Association of Field Ornithologists|Journal of Field Ornithology]] |date=Summer 1991 |volume=62 |issue=3 |page=344 |publisher=[[Wiley (publisher)|Wiley]]|jstor=20065800 }}</ref> The island was most notably owned by financier and sex offender [[Jeffrey Epstein]], along with the neighboring [[Little Saint James]] island.

The cove on the west side of Great Saint James, Christmas Cove, is a popular snorkeling and mooring spot for day charter boats and yachts. Twenty-two overnight mooring balls are available (but are not regularly maintained).<ref name=":1" /><ref name="ederNyt">{{cite web |last1=Eder |first1=Steve |title=Epstein's Island, 'Little St. Jeff's': A Hideaway Where Money Bought Influence |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/08/28/business/jeffrey-epstein-island.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |accessdate=6 November 2019 |date=28 August 2019}}</ref><ref name="apCoto">{{cite news |last1=Coto |first1=Dánica |title=Whispers, suspicion about Epstein on Caribbean island |url=https://apnews.com/cd794044e8be4e619093582d6d3355d2 |accessdate=November 6, 2019 |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=July 10, 2019}}</ref>

== Ownership ==

=== Before Epstein's ownership ===
Great Saint James was worth US$3 million at one point when a woman owned it.{{Citation needed|reason=Who?|date=December 2025}} She later died in a Swiss [[chalet]]. The island was subsequently divided into parcels and three people inherited it.<ref name="apCoto" />

Family members of the Danish politician {{ill|Christian Kjær|da}} had owned Great Saint James since the late 1970s.<ref name="miami" /> [[Miami Dolphins]] player [[Jason Taylor (American football)|Jason Taylor]] purchased the island with assistance from real estate businessmen Robert Addie and [[Jorge M. Pérez]] in 2004. However, a lawsuit exchange ensued and lasted until December 2013 when Taylor received "much but not all" of his [[down payment]], as reported by the ''[[Miami Herald]]''.<ref name="miami" />

=== Jeffrey Epstein ===
Great Saint James was purchased in 2016 for US$22.5 million by financier and sex offender [[Jeffrey Epstein]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.virginislandsdailynews.com/news/epstein-building-compound-on-great-st-james/article_a49261e9-40f0-57b1-9501-605e26e74cf3.html|title=Epstein building compound on Great St. James|last=Carlson|first=Suzanne|website=[[The Virgin Islands Daily News]]|language=en|access-date=2019-07-13|date=May 7, 2019}}</ref><ref name="miami">{{cite web |last1=Brown |first1=Julie K. |last2=Hall |first2=Kevin G. |authorlink1=Julie K. Brown |title=For Jeffrey Epstein, one island hideaway wasn't enough. How he stealthily acquired a second |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/news/state/florida/article235224877.html |website=[[Miami Herald]] |accessdate=6 November 2019 |date=October 1, 2019}}</ref> who already owned the neighboring [[Little Saint James]] island.<ref name="ederNyt" /> The Danish newspaper ''[[B.T. (tabloid)|B.T.]]'' has reported that at some point while Kjær owned {{convert|80.1|acre|ha}} of the island, Epstein had attempted to purchase the island, but that the sale had not gone through, partially because islanders "begged" Kjær and his wife Susan Astani not to sell the land to Epstein. Astani said that at the time there were rumors about Epstein's "sexual preferences".<ref name="miami" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bt.dk/kendte/susan-astani-havde-ubehagelig-oplevelse-med-afdoed-mangemillionaer|title= Susan Astani havde ubehagelig oplevelse med afdød mangemillionær|first1=Bo|last1=Poulsen|first2=Christian|last2=Hansen|date=2019-08-12|access-date=2019-08-12|work=[[B.T. (tabloid)|B.T.]]}}</ref> In order to conceal his identity, Epstein made [[Sultan Ahmed bin Sulayem]] the [[Beneficial ownership|ultimate beneficial owner]] against his will and purchased Kjær's three parcels through his [[shell corporation]] Great St. Jim LLC, for US$17.5 million on January 18, 2016.<ref name=":1" /><ref name="miami" /> He bought the rest of the island (twelve parcels totalling {{convert|81.22|acre|ha}}) through the same LLC from GSJ Properties Corp. for US$5 million on January 21, 2016.<ref name=":1" />

Epstein had been in conflict with the Virgin Islands Department of Planning and Natural Resources (DPNR) over land use regulations.<ref name=":1" /><ref name="ederNyt" /> DPNR Commissioner Jean-Pierre Oriol has said, "Since there's been an active owner of the island, there's been construction within three months of that, so it's been pretty active."<ref name="continuing">{{cite web |last1=Carlson |first1=Suzanne |title=Epstein continuing illegal construction on Great St. James despite stop-work order, threat of fines |url=http://www.virginislandsdailynews.com/news/epstein-continuing-illegal-construction-on-great-st-james-despite-stop/article_cb7c0fcc-89e2-5366-8dd2-23efa661f2f7.html |website=The Virgin Islands Daily News |accessdate=8 November 2019 |language=en |date=May 8, 2019}}</ref> Great St. Jim LLC has authorized several officers of Epstein's nonprofit Gratitude America Ltd. to act on behalf of Poplar Inc., whose president is Epstein according to an incumbency certificate, with respect to all transactions including those related to permitting matters.<ref name=":1" /> In April 2016, after DPNR received complaints about Epstein clearing the island without a permit, a [[cease and desist]] was ordered and Great St. Jim LLC was initially fined US$280,000, but Epstein settled for a US$70,000 fine.<ref name="miami" /><ref name="ederNyt" /> Epstein also sent US$320,000 in total in checks through his foundations to the non-profit [[Saint Thomas Historical Trust]] in order to circumvent fines by the government. However, Epstein had reportedly misunderstood an order to send a part of the settlement to a local preservation project.<ref name="deutsche">{{cite web |last1=Strasburg |first1=Jenny |last2=O’Brien |first2=Rebecca Davis |title=Jeffrey Epstein Used Opaque Charity Account at Deutsche Bank for Own Benefit |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/jeffrey-epstein-used-opaque-charity-account-at-deutsche-bank-for-own-benefit-11568286004 |website=Wall Street Journal |accessdate=7 November 2019 |date=September 12, 2019}}</ref> According to a lawyer for Epstein, the donations were returned to Epstein by DPNR employees in 2017. Historical Trust's president Malcolm Schweizer said in August 2019: "If any agreement was made with Epstein on behalf of the St. Thomas Historical Trust to return the funds, it was done fraudulently and without our knowledge. I still plan to pursue return of the entire $320,000 to the St. Thomas Historical Trust, and am awaiting the results of an investigation by the FBI before I take further action".<ref name="deutsche" /><ref>{{cite web |last=Carlson |first=Suzanne |title=DPNR never gave Historical Trust $320K in Epstein donations; Historical Trust asks feds to investigate |url=http://www.virginislandsdailynews.com/news/dpnr-never-gave-historical-trust-k-in-epstein-donations-historical/article_2d233d9d-ce57-547c-9133-fd585bdd734e.html |website=The Virgin Islands Daily News |accessdate=7 November 2019 |language=en |date=August 24, 2019}}</ref> Epstein was issued another cease and desist order by DPNR on October 28, 2016, for not permitted "development in the coastal zone".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Austin |first1=Jonathan |title=Corporation cited by DPNR for development on Great St. James Island |url=http://www.virginislandsdailynews.com/news/corporation-cited-by-dpnr-for-development-on-great-st-james/article_6a85722f-58a1-53e9-b208-4d8aaf0e77d4.html |website=The Virgin Islands Daily News |accessdate=8 November 2019 |language=en |date=November 4, 2016}}</ref>

''[[The Virgin Islands Daily News]]'' have reported communication between Epstein's staff and DPNR regarding building plan permits and permit applications. Documents and plans show a private road, "a barge dock, two homes, cottages, an amphitheater, gardens, a marine electrical cable, solar array and generator, storage building, security building, work-shed and machine shop and an 'underwater office & pool'. The permit application addresses mitigation efforts for endangered corals and the [[Chilabothrus monensis|Virgin Islands tree boa]], which was spotted on the island during site visits, and indicates that the public will still have free access to the island's shoreline, which includes Christmas Cove".<ref name=":1" /> According to ''[[New York (magazine)|New York magazine]]'', Epstein "shut down Christmas Cove" after he purchased the island.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://nymag.com/intelligencer/2019/07/everything-we-know-about-jeffrey-epsteins-private-islands.html|title=Everything We Know About Jeffrey Epstein's Private 'Pedophile Island'|last=Stieb|first=Matt|date=2019-07-10|website=[[New York (magazine)|New York]]|language=en|access-date=2019-07-13}}</ref>

On December 21, 2018, Epstein received a stop-work order from Coastal Zone Management.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="visit">{{cite web |last=Carlson |first=Suzanne |title=DPNR planning visit to Epstein's island |url=http://www.virginislandsdailynews.com/news/dpnr-planning-visit-to-epstein-s-island/article_2b432501-8f05-5f49-aae4-b985d340d5e6.html |website=The Virgin Islands Daily News |accessdate=November 6, 2019 |language=en |date=July 13, 2019}}</ref> He was subsequently accused of violating the order "by not removing a beach bar cabana and by expanding a driveway", according to ''[[The New York Times]]''.<ref name="ederNyt" /><ref name=":0" /> DPNR Commissioner Jean-Pierre Oriol has said that Epstein could be fined over US$1 million for construction activity including "an excessive amount of additional roadways that have been carved out on the island, [for] there have been two [[jetty|jetties]], fill material has been placed into the submerged lands, so there's evidence of work going beyond what was initially applied for. The exact amount of things is still yet to be determined". According to ''The Virgin Islands Daily News'', photos on social media showed construction work around June 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=Construction appears to continue on Great St. James |date=July 9, 2019 |last=Carlson |first=Suzanne |website=[[The Virgin Islands Daily News]] |language=en |access-date=2019-07-13 |url=http://www.virginislandsdailynews.com/news/construction-appears-to-continue-on-great-st-james/article_58f62584-cefe-5719-bef2-06d538ed2658.html}}</ref> By July 2019, Coastal Zone Management and Epstein's representatives agreed to a site visit for inspection. They had been working to resolve environmental issues such as those that had arisen from erosion and cutting a road. DPNR Assistant Commissioner Keith Richards said that "Epstein's representatives [had] applied for at least four minor permits", but that "only one minor permit for the construction of a flagpole and repair of cisterns [had] been approved". Coastal Zone Management ordered one of the jetties to be removed.<ref name="visit"/> Around July 2019, the [[United States Environmental Protection Agency]] visited Great Saint James.<ref>{{cite web |last=Carlson |first=Suzanne |title=Environmental Protection Agency visited Epstein's Great St. James island |url=http://www.virginislandsdailynews.com/news/environmental-protection-agency-visited-epstein-s-great-st-james-island/article_dad8a510-e057-5322-a944-36ac5551a3a9.html |website=The Virgin Islands Daily News |accessdate=8 November 2019 |language=en |date=July 25, 2019}}</ref>

Epstein was arrested in July 2019 and admitted in an affidavit that he owned Great Saint James.<ref name="miami" /> After [[Death of Jeffrey Epstein|Epstein's death]] in August 2019, multiple permits were still pending. A survey company owned by a civil engineering companies owner from [[Saint Croix]] applied for a temporary [[barge]] landing permit to allow construction work. The owner, Jeffrey Bateman, said of Epstein: "He just had a lot of money. People with a lot of money can buy islands".<ref name="miami" /> Epstein had not built anything on Great Saint James prior to his death.<ref>{{cite news |work=Associated Press |last1=Coto |first1=Dánica |title=Epstein's Caribbean islands drawing tourists after his death |url=https://apnews.com/15c9c4f6778d4116bd080422e1d12060 |accessdate=8 November 2019 |language=en |date=15 August 2019}}</ref>

Great Saint James and the neighboring Little Saint James were listed for sale at $125 million in March 2022. A lawyer for Epstein's estate stated that they planned to use the proceeds from the sale to settle a number of lawsuits. Bespoke Real Estate, the agency jointly overseeing the sale, stated that further information on the listing was only available to prospective buyers.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Clarke |first=Sarah Paynter and Katherine |date=2022-03-23 |title=Jeffrey Epstein's Private Islands in the Caribbean to List for $125 Million |language=en-US |work=Wall Street Journal |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/jeffrey-epsteins-private-islands-in-the-caribbean-to-list-for-125-million-11647998425 |access-date=2022-03-25 |issn=0099-9660}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-23 |title=Jeffrey Epstein's St. James Islands Listed For Sale |url=https://stthomassource.com/content/2022/03/23/jeffrey-epsteins-st-james-islands-listed-for-sale/ |access-date=2022-03-25 |website=St. Thomas Source |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== After Epstein's ownership ===
In May 2023, billionaire Stephen Deckoff, under his firm SD Investments, announced the acquisition of Great St. James and Little St. James for $60 million.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Dey |first1=Kunal |title=Stephen Deckoff: Billionaire acquires Jeffrey Epstein's private islands for $60 million |url=https://meaww.com/who-is-stephen-deckoff-billionaire-acquires-jeffrey-epsteins-private-islands-for-60-million |website=Meaww.com |access-date=November 23, 2025 |date=May 4, 2023 |quote=Deckoff acquired the properties for less than half of their $125M initial asking price}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Goldstein |first=Matthew |date=May 3, 2023 |title=Billionaire Investor Buys Epstein's Private Islands for $60 Million |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/05/03/business/epstein-islands-sale.html |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251031113121/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/05/03/business/epstein-islands-sale.html |archive-date=October 31, 2025 |access-date=December 30, 2025 |work=The New York Times}}</ref>

The island is approximately 165 acres (67 ha) in size, and is located 0.4 kilometres (0.25 mi) southeast of Saint Thomas. The island was most notably owned by financier and sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, along with the neighboring Little Saint James island.
The cove on the west side of Great Saint James, Christmas Cove, is a popular snorkeling and mooring spot for day charter boats and yachts. Twenty-two overnight mooring balls are available (but are not regularly maintained).
